slides.label: THE FIRST ONE
slides.headline: A Bolton Repairman's Idea
slides.credit: Photo: Museumsfoto / CC BY 3.0 de via Wikimedia Commons
slides.body: John Harwood made the first self-winding wristwatch. Rolex named him its inventor in 1956.

slides.label: HOW IT WORKS
slides.headline: Each Swing Tightens A Spring
slides.credit: Photo: Hustvedt / CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons
slides.body: A weight swings about 230 degrees as you move, winding the spring that stores power.

slides.label: SEE IT WORK
slides.headline: You Can See It Work
slides.credit: Photo: Hustvedt / CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons
slides.body: A skeleton dial shows the parts moving.
Comment: do you wind your watch, or let it wind itself?
